active_questions.q: What is the current state of work on representing proofs as structured objects, and how does the eight-role proof-graph vocabulary relate to it?
Which further classical proofs contain algorithm capsules, and which domains should the ATAP corpus cover next?
What methods exist for measuring structural similarity between labeled directed graphs, so 'family resemblance' becomes measurable rather than visible?
How have formal methods been applied to biological and other non-mathematical systems, and what did those applications actually yield?

frontier.open: Whether the algorithm-capsule regularity is a real structural feature of mathematics or an artifact of how these three proofs were encoded
frontier.why: The paper's central empirical claim rests on n=3. A family of three could be selection effect: capsules were found because capsules were sought. No literature settles this — it needs more entries encoded without looking for capsules, or an independent encoder.

frontier.open: Whether the eight-role node vocabulary is adequate as the corpus grows, or will need roles it does not yet have
frontier.why: A vocabulary that never needs revision may be under-tested rather than correct. Only encoding unfamiliar proof types reveals this.

frontier.open: Whether Mermaid graph representation is right for mathematics, or the most-used method mistaken for the only one
frontier.why: Constitution anti-hammer clause aimed at this project. The Methods Catalog says Mermaid distorts what is not nodes-and-edges — magnitude, continuity, uncertainty. Which mathematical content is lost, and what would render it? Answering requires trying an alternative on a real proof, not reading about alternatives.

frontier.open: Whether pointing mathematical structure at an under-mathematized domain produces genuine discovery or sophisticated re-description — GLMP being the first test
frontier.why: The mother-lode question for the whole mathematics initiative. GLMP and this project are already one bridge — the same Programming Framework applied to gene-regulatory logic and to justificatory structure, two domains sharing no subject matter. The claim only holds if formalizing a domain yields something that was not visible before it; a re-description that predicts nothing new is a marked limit, not a finding.

frontier.open: Whether the graph representation preserves what makes a proof beautiful, or strips exactly that out
frontier.why: The sharper, empirically approachable form of the mathematics/feeling boundary question. If the diagonal move's beauty is structural, the graph should carry it — strong evidence for the representation. If beauty is precisely the residue that does not survive encoding, that is a limit with teeth. Either answer is a finding; neither is in the literature.

horizons: formal verification and proof assistant libraries (Lean mathlib, Coq, Isabelle)
category theory and string diagrams as alternative representations
machine learning over graph-structured mathematical objects
automated theorem proving and proof search
mathematical structure in music and its emotional effect
cognitive science of mathematical intuition and elegance
